description:
FILED s1061 (Opus, 2026-09-07) from the s474 CPAN-board delta: three of the
six newly-failing Scalar-List-Utils rows (sum.t 9/10/11, product.t 14/15/16)
are ONE pre-existing runtime bug, uncovered by #1508 letting the files reach
their Math::BigInt section.

  scalar(EXPR) where EXPR is a HASH REFERENCE returns the RAW hash table,
  dropping the reference.

`p-scalar` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp ~line 22727) dispatches on the UNBOXED value:

    ((and (vectorp v) (adjustable-array-p v))
     (if (p-box-p val) val (length v)))         ; array: box preserved
    ((and (hash-table-p v) (not (p-box-p val))) (%p-hash-user-count v))
    ...
    (t v)                                        ; <- a BOXED hash lands here

The array arm was fixed (its own comment says "The hash branch below already
carries exactly this (not (p-box-p val)) guard; the array branch never got
it") -- but the hash arm only DECLINES for a boxed hash; it never returns the
box, so the fall-through `(t v)` hands back the bare hash table.  Rule 11:
two copies of one rule, one of them repaired.

SYMPTOMS (probed vs perl 5.40.3):

  { package H; use overload '""' => sub { "H<".$_[0]{v}.">" }, fallback => 1;
    sub new { my ($c,$v)=@_; bless {v=>$v}, $c } }
  my $h = H->new(9);
  print scalar($h), "\n";              # perl H<9>      PCL HASH(0x1)
  my $c = scalar($h); print "$c\n";    # perl H<9>      PCL 1     <-- KEY COUNT
  print ref($c), "\n";                 # perl H         PCL ""

  my $a = { v => 9 };                  # unblessed, same fault
  my $ca = scalar($a); print ref($ca); # perl HASH      PCL ""

`ref(scalar($h))` still answers "H" (ref() reads a raw hash table as a
hashref), which is why this hid: only stringification and assignment show it.
An overloaded class loses its `""` handler because the handler is found from
the REFERENCE, and a blessed SCALAR ref (the p-box-is-ref path) is unaffected
-- only the aggregate spelling breaks.

WHERE IT BITES ON THE BOARD: `is($v, $v1 + $v2, 'bigint')` -- an arithmetic
expression in an ARGUMENT slot is lowered `(p-scalar (p-+ $v1 $v2))`, so
Math::BigInt's result reaches `is` as a bare hash table and the expected side
prints `HASH(0x4)` while the got side is the right 73786976294838206463.
Six rows: Scalar-List-Utils t/sum.t 9-11 and t/product.t 14-16 (perl: 18/0
and 27/0).

REPRODUCE (the SYMPTOMS block above is the whole file -- write it to /tmp/s.pl):
    diff <(./runpcl /tmp/s.pl) <(perl /tmp/s.pl)
    perl tools/run-dist-t.pl --no-dist-lib ~/.cpan/build/Scalar-List-Utils-1.70-0 t/sum.t

SHAPE OF THE FIX (not taken here -- s1061's resume brief is "no new fix"):
give the hash arm the array arm's shape,

    ((hash-table-p v) (if (p-box-p val) val (%p-hash-user-count v)))

and delete the now-redundant `(not (p-box-p val))` guard.  Bars: the fix
changes only the runtime, so it owes the full sweep and the op/ companion leg
(a coercion change), plus guard rows -- the four spellings above, with the
unblessed one, and the `scalar(@array)` / `scalar(%hash)` negatives that must
NOT move.

=== DONE (s473w, 2026-09-09) ===

SHIPPED as the task's own sketch: the hash arm gets the array arm's shape,

    ((hash-table-p v) (if (p-box-p val) val (%p-hash-user-count v)))

and the `%ENV`/`%INC` MARKER arm gets it too (a boxed marker is a hash ref to
%ENV and must not be dereferenced either).  The redundant `(not (p-box-p val))`
guards are gone.  `cl/pcl-runtime.lisp` only; no emission change beyond the
generation bump the batch's #1507 needed.

PROBED vs perl 5.40.3, nine lines, byte-identical after the fix and wrong in
four of them before (A `HASH(0x1)`, B `1`, C `''`, D `''`):

    A: scalar($h) stringified          H<9>
    B: my $c = scalar($h); "$c"        H<9>
    C: ref($c)                         H
    D: ref(scalar({v=>9}))             HASH
    E-I negatives, unmoved:  scalar(@{[1,2,3]})=3, scalar(%g)=2,
                             scalar(@ar)=3, scalar(%ENV)>0, ref(scalar(\%g))=HASH

WHY THE EXISTING GUARD DID NOT CATCH IT â the finding worth keeping.
`Pl/t/tap-assert-01.t`'s section 7 already asserted `ref(scalar($hr))` eq HASH
and PASSED, because its `$hr = \%h` and `p-backslash` sets the box's `is-ref`
flag, so that spelling was caught by `p-scalar`'s REF arm two branches earlier.
A `{â¦}` CONSTRUCTOR sets no flag (a box wrapping a hash table is unambiguously
a ref), so only the constructor spelling was broken â and `ref()` reads a raw
hash table as HASH, so the bug hid behind a passing `ref()` and showed only in
stringification and assignment.

GUARD: `Pl/t/tap-assert-01.t` section 7b (row 23), inverse-verified on a
`0ece3088` extraction.  ir-spec Â§2.4 states the rule normatively beside Â§2.3's
array twin.  Commit `c07d0100`.
subject: SILENT WRONG (pre-existing): `scalar(EXPR)` on a HASH REFERENCE returns the RAW hash table -- an overloaded object loses its `""` handler (prints HASH(0x1)) and `my $c = scalar($href)` stores the KEY COUNT; the array arm of p-scalar was repaired and the hash arm was not (Scalar-List-Utils sum.t 9-11 + product.t 14-16)
